pr.title: Apply effects to `otherwise` edge in dataflow analysis
pr.description:
This allows `ElaborateDrops` to remove drops when a `match` wildcard arm covers multiple no-Drop enum variants. It modifies dataflow analysis to update the `MaybeUninitializedPlaces` and `MaybeInitializedPlaces` data for a block reached through an `otherwise` edge.

Fixes rust-lang/rust#142705.
pr.author: ashivaram23

issues.title: Drop is called for match wildcards even when all matched variants have no Drop
issues.body:
Consider matching on an enum where multiple variants should match to the same expression. Those variants can be explicitly spelled out in one or more match arms, or they can be grouped with the wildcard pattern `_` instead.

In some cases, spelling out the variants (ideally in a single arm with a pattern like `Variant1 | Variant2`) can generate smaller LLVM IR compared to the wildcard version, and less frequently can generate better machine code. One way this can happen is when another variant in a different match arm has a nontrivial `Drop` but the groupable variants don't. The optimized MIR will still try to drop the whole enum or check for the variants that need `Drop`, potentially leading to larger LLVM IR that takes longer for LLVM to process or results in worse machine code.

---

Here is a simple example, a function that converts a container with multiple full and empty variants to an `Option`:

```rust
pub enum Container {
    Empty1,
    Empty2,
    Full1(String),
    Full2(String),
}

pub fn into_option(container: Container) -> Option<String> {
    match container {
        Container::Full1(s) | Container::Full2(s) => Some(s),
        Container::Empty1 | Container::Empty2 => None,
        // _ => None,
    }
}
```

Both approaches generate similar machine code with `opt-level=3`, but the initial LLVM IR is significantly larger with the wildcard.

---

Another example is a `take` function for a container that panics if it's "locked":

```rust
pub enum Container {
    Empty,
    Locked,
    Full(String),
}

pub fn take(container: &mut Container) -> Option<String> {
    match container {
        Container::Empty => None,
        Container::Locked => panic!("you tried to break into the container!"),
        Container::Full(_) => match std::mem::replace(container, Container::Empty) {
            Container::Full(content) => Some(content),
            Container::Empty | Container::Locked => unreachable!(),
            // _ => unreachable!(),
        },
    }
}
```

This time, in addition to larger LLVM IR, the final machine code is larger and contains an unnecessary unreachable check when using `panic_unwind`. (With `panic_abort`, the LLVM IR is very similar in both cases. The wildcard machine code still contains the unreachable check, but that's a different issue that seems more suited to the LLVM side.)

(Note that if `Locked` becomes `Locked(String)` so that it needs `Drop`, the machine code will contain the unreachable check no matter how you write the match arms when using `panic_unwind`. That might be better characterized as an LLVM improvement, but I'm mentioning it because an LLVM opt improvement fixing that might also fix the case above without any MIR opt changes. I haven't looked into it though.)

processing.reason: The historical bug is a missed optimization, not an observable semantic mistake. Before the patch, the `otherwise` edge simply left the dataflow state unchanged: explicitly handled variants stayed maybe-initialized and were not marked maybe-uninitialized. That can make `ElaborateDrops` retain an extra whole-enum drop (or a conditional drop flag) on a wildcard arm, and can make `RemoveUninitDrops` fail to remove that drop. But the PR’s precondition is exactly that the wildcard-reachable variants have no drop-requiring fields. Dropping such an active variant is a no-op; retained drops are expanded with discriminant switches that cannot run destructors for inactive/moved variants. Producing different return values would require adding a destructor side effect to a wildcard variant, which violates the historical precondition and would instead test a different rewrite (removing a required drop). Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed pair with differing concrete outputs can faithfully model this PR.

analysis.summary: SwitchInt dataflow edge effects must be applied to the `otherwise` target, not only to explicit discriminant targets. ElaborateDrops and RemoveUninitDrops consume MaybeInitializedPlaces/MaybeUninitializedPlaces; without otherwise-edge effects, variants actually excluded by the wildcard arm remain maybe-live and drop elaboration keeps avoidable enum drops. The fix models otherwise-edge inactive variants as the list of explicitly handled discriminants and kills (initialized) or gens (uninitialized) their move paths.
analysis.originalLogic: In `Analysis::apply_switch_int_edge_effect`, dataflow only handled `SwitchTargetValue::Normal(value)`: it computed the single active variant with `data.next_discr(value)` and called `drop_flag_effects::on_all_inactive_variants(..., active_variant, ...)`, killing all other variants' move paths for MaybeInitializedPlaces and gen'ing them for MaybeUninitializedPlaces. For `SwitchTargetValue::Otherwise`, the implementation returned without changing the dataflow state. Thus, on the wildcard/otherwise edge of an enum discriminant switch, every variant that was explicitly matched by a normal switch target was still treated as possibly initialized/uninitialized, so ElaborateDrops could not prove that the remaining wildcard variants require no drop. The patch's comment describes this as: "Once we get to the final, \"otherwise\" branch, there is no need to preserve `exit_state`, so pass it directly to `apply_switch_int_edge_effect` to save a clone of the dataflow state."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical behavior: when propagating dataflow state to a block reached through `SwitchTargetValue::Otherwise`, the analysis skipped inactive-variant effects entirely. As a result, the wildcard arm's target kept all explicitly handled variants as maybe-initialized (and not definitely uninitialized), so ElaborateDrops retained `drop(_1)` / cleanup drops for the whole enum on that path. The corrected transformation computes `InactiveVariants::Inactives(data.variants(targets))` for the otherwise edge, where `variants` maps `targets.all_values()` through `next_discr`, and then applies `on_all_inactive_variants`: MaybeInitializedPlaces kills those move paths, MaybeUninitializedPlaces gen's them. This is guarded by new opt-in flags `exclude_inactive_in_otherwise` and `include_inactive_in_otherwise`, enabled by ElaborateDrops and `exclude_inactive_in_otherwise` by RemoveUninitDrops. The incorrect result is therefore extra drops on otherwise paths, not removal of a required drop; do not construct a test that simply deletes a drop for a variant containing Drop fields.
analysis.inputDomain: Enums (or `Result`-like ADTs) matched by a `SwitchInt` on the discriminant, where the `otherwise` target corresponds to a wildcard `_` arm or grouped wildcard covering one or more variants that have no drop-requiring fields, while another variant has a field requiring Drop. The regression test uses `Result<String, ()>`: `match result { Ok(s) => Some(s), _ => None }`, compiled with `-C panic=abort`. The issue's motivating example is an enum with `Empty1`, `Empty2`, `Full1(String)`, `Full2(String)` and `Container::Full1(s) | Container::Full2(s) => Some(s), _ => None`. The behavior concerns the MIR/dataflow state on the `otherwise` edge, including cleanup paths, not the normal `Ok`/`Full` discriminant edges.
analysis.trigger: A `SwitchInt` terminator on an enum discriminant has an `otherwise` target, and the edge-effect analysis is reached with `SwitchTargetValue::Otherwise`. The bug manifests when variants excluded by that otherwise edge are explicitly listed in `targets` and have no move paths requiring drops on the wildcard path; the old code leaves them maybe-initialized, causing ElaborateDrops to emit/retain drops for the whole enum. The fix is only applied for analyses opting in via `exclude_inactive_in_otherwise` / `include_inactive_in_otherwise`.
preconditions: The match lowers to a `SwitchInt` on the enum discriminant with an `otherwise` target.
At least one variant is handled by an explicit normal switch target and is therefore definitely inactive on the otherwise edge.
The variants reachable through the otherwise edge do not require the drop that was previously retained (for example, unit variants or no-Drop fields).

The dataflow analysis is MaybeInitializedPlaces with `exclude_inactive_in_otherwise` or MaybeUninitializedPlaces with `include_inactive_in_otherwise`; ElaborateDrops enables both, and RemoveUninitDrops enables the MaybeInitializedPlaces flag.

`on_all_inactive_variants` only calls the handler for child move paths that exist for a variant: the patch notes "If there are no move paths corresponding to an inactive variant, `handle_inactive_variant` will not be called for that variant."
pitfalls: Do not generalize the old behavior as "otherwise edge is ignored for all analyses": the new flags make the effect opt-in, so analyses that do not opt in still return early for `SwitchTargetValue::Otherwise`.

Do not mark all variants inactive on an otherwise edge; only the variants represented by `targets.all_values()` are known inactive. Variants reachable only through the otherwise branch must remain live.

For backward dataflow, `switch_sources` supplies values but no discriminant value for the otherwise branch; the patch passes the full `mir::SwitchTargets` into `apply_switch_int_edge_effect` and uses `targets` to recover the inactive list.

`MaybePlacesSwitchIntData::variants` resets `self.index = 0` and maps `targets.all_values()` in order; `next_discr` relies on the comment that "The discriminant order in the `SwitchInt` targets should match the order yielded by `AdtDef::discriminants`."

The correction changes two complementary domains in opposite directions: initialized places kill inactive paths, uninitialized places gen inactive paths. Do not apply only one side when testing ElaborateDrops.

Do not conflate this drop-elaboration fix with SROA: the `sroa/lifetimes.foo.ScalarReplacementOfAggregates.diff` update is an expectation change showing altered drop/switch structure, not a separate SROA-specific rule.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a MIR-opt test with `//@ compile-flags: -C panic=abort`, `//@ test-mir-pass: ElaborateDrops`, and `// EMIT_MIR otherwise_drops.result_ok.ElaborateDrops.diff`, as in `tests/mir-opt/otherwise_drops.rs`. The source is `fn result_ok(result: Result<String, ()>) -> Option<String> { match result { Ok(s) => Some(s), _ => None } }` with `// CHECK-NOT: drop`; the retained test comment says: "Ensures there are no drops for the wildcard match arm." Build the comparison as two otherwise-identical programs: one with wildcard `_` covering no-Drop variants and one spelling out those variants explicitly; verify the wildcard MIR no longer contains the whole-enum drop on the otherwise path while the `Ok` path still drops/moves correctly. Add a negative control where the otherwise-reachable variant contains a `String`/Drop field and assert its drop is preserved. Also exercise RemoveUninitDrops, because it uses `MaybeInitializedPlaces::new(...).exclude_inactive_in_otherwise()`. Inspect the supplied diff: before the fix `bb5` contains `drop(_1) -> [return: bb6, unwind: bb9]` and cleanup `drop(_1)` in `bb8`; after the fix these become `goto -> bb16` and `goto -> bb9`, with new discriminant re-checks (`_6 = discriminant(_1); switchInt(move _6) -> [0: bb13, otherwise: bb14]`) deciding whether a drop is needed.
